turns.content: Before constructing a quantum evolution, compute the adjoints of X=(i,-1,2i; 1,0,1; 2i,-1,-i) and Z=(3,2i,5; -2i,-2,-4i; 5,4i,4). Classify each and state the relation between X and X-dagger.
Set U=exp(X). Use the adjoint relation just obtained to determine whether U is unitary and therefore norm-preserving.
As a separate benchmark transformation, check W=(0,0,1; 0,1,0; 1,0,0) directly against the unitary condition.
Now take Y=(0.5,0.1,0.2; 0.1,0.25,0.1; 0.2,0.1,0.25). Test whether it is a density matrix by checking Hermiticity, trace, and positive semidefiniteness.
Apply the evolution chosen earlier to the state candidate introduced in the preceding step. Write the resulting state using the matrices actually available, and determine whether it is valid.
Determine from the available information whether the transformation used above is unitary. State which state properties follow only when that premise holds.
Summarize the classifications reached for the objects actually introduced, making any conclusion conditional when the required matrix information is incomplete.
